analyst_view.overall: Osasuna (16th, 12 pts) host bottom side Málaga (20th, 5 pts, one win in their last 13 games in all competitions) on Sunday evening in a game both badly need. Osasuna are unbeaten in their last three at home; Budimir is fit after Croatia duty, Sergio Herrera replaces the injured Aitor Fernández in goal and Diego Rico covers for Bretones (both in the numbers), while winger Del Castillo is still listed as a doubt, which the numbers do not know. Málaga have Aznou suspended and miss Rafita, Lobete and Ochoa (in the numbers); Murillo is back training with the group, and they have scored in six straight games but lost their last two. No referee had been named in the pages I read.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals and already give Málaga a small boost for Bretones being out. Osasuna have scored only 12 in 12 and are likely without Del Castillo, one of their main creators, which the numbers don't know, and a nervous relegation game tends to be cautious. A small lean down to about 2.7.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.3 corners, with both sides' recent corner counts already counted. Osasuna lean on crosses from Rubén García and Moi Gómez for Budimir, which brings corners, but losing Del Castillo on the wing could reduce them a little; it balances out. I stay at 10.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards; they add Osasuna's recent cards (19 in six) and take some off for Málaga's quieter run, but make no adjustment for the stakes. A relegation fight against a bottom side that must take risks tends to be scrappy, and Málaga already lost Aznou to a ban. A small lean up to about 4.8; no referee named yet.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.6 shots and already add a lot for both sides' recent shooting and how much each concedes (+11% each). Del Castillo's likely absence and a nervy game point a little lower, but Budimir being fit and Málaga needing to attack point the other way, so I stay at 30.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target. Budimir is fit after the break, as the numbers assume, and Málaga's recent accuracy (33 on target in six) is already counted. No clear reason to move it, so 9.6.
